meeting.title: beehiiv semantic layer working session — fct_subscriptions
meeting.summary: Working session on the first metrics block. Aisha delivered all three access prerequisites within two days of kickoff, so Theo had the repo connected and a clean dbt compile running before the call. The session was spent on fct_subscriptions naming, and Aisha's prediction was correct — growth and finance have materially different definitions of an active subscriber, differing on whether to include subscribers in a payment-failure grace period. The metrics block is on hold until Marcus rules. Everything else on the semantic layer progressed.
action_items: Marcus to rule on whether payment-failure grace-period subscribers count as active
Aisha to pull the numbers both ways so the decision is made against real figures rather than opinion
Theo to land the uncontested metrics on fct_subscriptions and leave active_subscribers stubbed
Theo to set up CI checks on semantic layer changes
key_decisions: Uncontested metrics ship now; active_subscribers is stubbed pending Marcus's ruling
Grace-period definition will be decided against real numbers, not in the abstract
CI checks go in before any dashboard migration begins
meeting.notes: Night and day compared to some accounts — Aisha turned around all three access requests in under 48 hours and the project compiled clean first try. The active_subscriber dispute is exactly the fight she predicted at kickoff. Blocking the metrics block on it is the right call; shipping a metric that two departments disagree on would poison the semantic layer on day one.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Before anything else — Aisha, you got us all three access items in two days. That is genuinely the fastest turnaround we've had this year.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Diallo
transcript.text: It's not hard when nobody's in the way.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: It made a real difference. Repo's connected, project compiles clean, all hundred and eleven models. No warnings worth mentioning.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Then let's spend the time on the thing you flagged at kickoff. fct_subscriptions.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Diallo
transcript.text: Right. So I went and pulled every definition of active subscriber currently in production. There are four. Two of them are the same thing written differently, which leaves two that genuinely disagree.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: What's the axis of disagreement?

transcript.speaker: Aisha Diallo
transcript.text: Grace period. When a subscriber's card fails we keep serving them for fourteen days while we retry. Growth counts those people as active — they're reading the newsletter, they're engaged. Finance does not — no money has arrived.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: And both are defensible, which is what makes it a real dispute rather than a bug.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Diallo
transcript.text: Exactly. Growth isn't wrong. Finance isn't wrong. But the executive dashboard can't show two different subscriber counts with the same label.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: How big is the gap in practice? If it's a rounding error nobody will fight about it.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Diallo
transcript.text: I don't have the number in front of me. I'd guess low single digit percent but I genuinely don't know, and I don't want to guess in a room where it might get quoted.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Then let's get the number before the argument. Can you pull it both ways?

transcript.speaker: Aisha Diallo
transcript.text: Yes. Give me a day.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: That's the right shape. Marcus said at kickoff he'd own the ruling — this is the first thing to send him, with both numbers attached. A decision against real figures is a decision. A decision in the abstract is a preference.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: So what do I do with the metrics block in the meantime? I don't want to sit on my hands.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Diallo
transcript.text: Most of the metrics aren't disputed. Churn, MRR, new subscriptions, reactivations — nobody argues about those.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Then I'll land the uncontested ones and stub active_subscribers with a comment pointing at the open decision. The moment Marcus rules, it's a one-line change.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Good. And put the CI checks in now, before any migration starts — I don't want a semantic layer change landing without a test once the dashboards depend on it.

transcript.speaker: Theo Okonkwo
transcript.text: Already scoped. That's this week.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Diallo
transcript.text: This is the conversation I've been trying to have internally for a year, incidentally. It took an external party asking the question.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: It usually does. Nobody wants to be the one who reopens a definition everyone's quietly been living with.
